name: NJ-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+10 district with strong Democratic fundamentals
Norcross's large financial advantage ($2.4M cash vs ~$5K)
Incumbent seeking re-election with no adverse headlines
model.rationale: The district's D+10 lean, Norcross's incumbency and overwhelming fundraising edge, and Polymarket pricing near 94% all point to a comfortable Democratic hold; the challenger's negligible resources leave little path to an upset.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a much tighter race or major outside spending against Norcross would warrant moving this toward Likely D.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
South Jersey's first district leans Democratic by about ten points, and incumbent Donald Norcross is seeking another term with every structural advantage intact. He has raised roughly $1.7 million and holds about $2.4 million on hand, while Republican Damon Galdo has raised barely $11,000, leaving the challenger without the resources to run a competitive campaign. No independent spending targets the incumbent, and no adverse headlines have surfaced.

Prediction markets put Norcross's chances in the mid-nineties, consistent with the district's fundamentals. With no public polling available, the forecast rests on partisan lean, incumbency, and money, all of which point the same direction. A Democratic hold is the clear expectation, though the absence of polling keeps uncertainty somewhat elevated.
